target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures establish the segment reporting framework, stating that information is consistent with the chief operating decision maker's view and identifying the existence of four reportable business units.

Both disclosures define the Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU) and the specific markets it serves (data center/PC/graphics/networking vs client/cloud server/enterprise/graphics/networking), representing the same underlying segment entity.

Both disclosures define the Mobile Business Unit (MBU) and its focus on smartphone and mobile-device markets.

Both disclosures define the Embedded Business Unit (EBU) and its focus on automotive, industrial, and consumer markets (intelligent edge).

Both disclosures define the Storage Business Unit (SBU) and its focus on SSDs/component-level solutions for enterprise/cloud and consumer markets.

previous_disclosures.summary: The company identifies four reportable business units: Compute and Networking (CNBU), Mobile (MBU), Embedded (EBU), and Storage (SBU), each comprising specific memory, storage, and networking products for defined markets.

current_disclosures.summary: Segment information is consistent with how it is reviewed and evaluated by the chief operating decision maker, with four reportable business units identified.
The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets.
The Mobile Business Unit includes memory and storage products sold into the smartphone and other mobile-device markets.
The Embedded Business Unit includes memory and storage products and solutions sold into the intelligent edge through the automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets.
The Storage Business Unit includes SSDs and component-level storage solutions sold into the data center, PC, and consumer markets.

materiality_analysis.reason: The company's four reportable segments (CNBU, MBU, EBU, SBU) remain unchanged. The changes are stylistic rewording and terminology adjustments: CNBU markets shifted from 'client, cloud server, enterprise' to 'data center...'; EBU added 'intelligent edge' and 'embedded'; SBU specified 'component-level' and 'data center'. These describe the same underlying business units and markets without introducing new segments or altering the strategic reporting framework.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 Embedded Business Unit (EBU) was a standalone segment. In 2025, the company reorganized into four segments, and the 'Embedded' function was merged into the 'Automotive and Embedded Business Unit' (AEBU) alongside the Automotive unit. No 2025 disclosure exists for a standalone 'Embedded Business Unit' matching the 2024 specific definition, as the entity itself was dissolved into a combined segment. Therefore, no direct counterpart is found.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD define specific reportable segments or business units focused on embedded applications. MU’s Embedded Business Unit (EBU) is defined by selling memory and storage products into the intelligent edge via automotive, industrial, and consumer markets. Similarly, AMD defines an Embedded segment that includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, and System on Modules (SOMs). While MU focuses on storage/memory for the edge and AMD focuses on computing processors for embedded systems, both explicitly identify an embedded-focused reporting unit covering similar end markets like automotive and industrial.

comparisons.comparison: MU and AVGO both disclose semiconductor solutions targeting the automotive and industrial markets, although structured differently. MU reports these under its Embedded Business Unit (EBU) focusing on memory and storage. AVGO reports these products under its Semiconductor Solutions segment, stating it provides products for the general industrial and automotive markets. Both identify automotive and industrial markets as key verticals for their embedded/edge semiconductor offerings.

comparisons.peer_summary: Business is organized into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All other; CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry are reportable operating segments, while NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable segments with selective disclosure.
comparisons.comparison: INTC does not have a standalone 'Embedded' business unit in its 2024 reportable segments, unlike MU, AMD, and NVDA. Instead, INTC organizes its business into Client Computing Group (CCG), Data Center and AI (DCAI), and Network and Edge (NEX), with non-reportable segments including Mobileye and Altera. While INTC’s Network and Edge segment may overlap with embedded/edge computing, it is not defined as an explicit 'Embedded' segment comparable to MU’s EBU. The other peers (AMD, NVDA, AVGO) have more direct parallels in defining specific embedded or edge-focused segments containing automotive/industrial products.

comparisons.comparison: MU and NVDA both disclose business segments that encompass automotive and embedded computing solutions. MU’s Embedded Business Unit sells memory and storage solutions into the automotive and intelligent edge markets. NVDA’s Compute & Networking segment explicitly includes automotive artificial intelligence, autonomous driving solutions, and Jetson for robotics and other embedded platforms. Both companies identify automotive and embedded/edge computing as distinct, significant components of their business operations, though MU’s scope is storage/memory-centric while NVDA’s is computing/AI-centric.
